record.original_question: Construct non-elementary holomorphic foliations F on Pk with leaves of dimension greater than 1 such that no leaf contains a compact curve.

evidence.quote: Problem 10.2. Construct non-elementary foliations F in Pk with leaves of dimension larger than 1 and such that every leaf does not contain a compact curve.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{P}^k$ denote complex projective space of dimension $k\ge 3$. A (singular) holomorphic foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^k$ of dimension $d$, with $1<d<k$, is given by an integrable holomorphic subbundle (twisted by a line bundle) of the tangent bundle of $\mathbb{P}^k$ defined off an analytic subset $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$ of codimension at least $2$; equivalently, by a global twisted holomorphic $d$-vector field that is locally decomposable and integrable. The foliation $\mathcal{F}$ is called elementary if it admits a non-constant meromorphic first integral, or, more generally, if it is a pull-back of a foliation of the same dimension on a lower-dimensional projective manifold via a rational map, or is invariant under a non-trivial algebraic group action — i.e., if it can be reduced to a lower-dimensional or homogeneous situation. Otherwise $\mathcal{F}$ is said to be non-elementary.

Problem: Exhibit a non-elementary holomorphic foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^k$ whose leaves have complex dimension strictly greater than $1$ and such that no leaf of $\mathcal{F}$ contains a compact (complex) algebraic curve.
artifact.status_search_result: No published construction of such non-elementary higher-dimensional holomorphic foliations on $\mathbb{P}^k$ with no compact curve in any leaf was located. The problem appears in a recent survey on higher-dimensional holomorphic foliations as an explicit open construction problem, and no resolution was found in the literature search.
